provisional: Which model serves which class comes from the research in docs/dynamic-model-research.md. Its independent numbers were read from search summaries, not from the leaderboards themselves, and found no specialist below 64 GB: so the class (fastest, balanced, strongest) decides, and the strengths are seeds you can edit. Speeds are measured on a Snapdragon X NPU by the app and replaced by what your PC measures.

S.name: Qwen3-1.7B (native NPU bundle)
S.note: Runs fully on the NPU; instant replies. Measured by the app.

S.name: Qwen3.5-4B
S.note: Best generalist of its size on the independent index (two versions agree); part of it runs on the CPU. Vision on the NPU gave wrong output once, so check it.

S.name: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507
S.note: Runs fully on the NPU; the app's own snake test passed.

M.name: Qwen3-1.7B (native NPU bundle)
M.note: Instant replies, fully on the NPU. Measured by the app.

M.name: LFM2.5-8B-A1B
M.note: Only 1B of its 8B is active, so it is fast; 64K context verified in the app. Weak on independent reasoning scores.

M.name: Qwen3.5-9B
M.note: Best under 10B on the independent index at launch, but its rank flips between index versions. The repo name is a guess and the speed an estimate (memory bandwidth ÷ file size): the app measures the real one.
